description: This bar chart, titled “The Unseen Targets of Hate -- A Systematic Review of Hateful Communication Datasets,” illustrates the number of datasets published each year from 2012 to 2021, categorized by the number of languages they contain. The horizontal axis represents the year, with labels for each year from 2012 to 2021. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of datasets,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^1 (10) to 10^2 (100), with tick marks at intervals of 10. The chart uses two colors to distinguish between datasets: blue bars represent datasets containing one language, and orange bars represent datasets containing two or more languages. For each year, there are two bars, one blue and one orange, except for the year 2021, which has a light blue bar and a small orange bar, and the year 2020, which has a blue bar and an orange bar. The blue bars are generally taller than the orange bars, indicating that datasets with one language are more common than those with two or more languages. The number of datasets increases over time, with the highest number of datasets (approximately 100) occurring in 2021 for the one-language category. The chart does not show any bars for the year 2022. The legend in the top left corner indicates that blue corresponds to “1” language and orange corresponds to “2+” languages.
